challenge.better_approach: Carrying the reading across a moved fingerprint would hide the expiry, which is the Law 3 answer the store already gives. Refusing the reseal blocks a legitimate act. Raising a trouble per voided ticket is heavier than the moment needs, since the seal's own output is read by the hand that will cross next. Printing at the writer is the smallest move.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the standing record before the run is the one the hollow was taken over. record_hollow lands on the standing record, so it is.
challenge.prior_art: persist_validation carries evidence.hollow only on an unchanged fingerprint; clearance.py names the retake command at hollow_evidence_absent. Nothing tells the seal's caller. Checked the tester and validation_store charters and the tickets corpus for 'hollow voided'; none.
challenge.real_collision: None. The tester charter's seal door keeps its exit codes; the PERSISTED line test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped reads is untouched.

answers.falsifier: Done when sealing a proof whose standing record carries a scratch ticket's hollow, after its code moved, prints that ticket and the retake command and exits 0, while the same seal over unchanged code carries the hollow and names nobody. Wrong intent if a voided hollow must block the reseal rather than be announced.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ordered it from five hollow_evidence_absent bounces measured 2026-11-12, among them 59f7 and d692 (cc_0's report) and 3195; the drop is persist_validation's fingerprint-gated carry at cairn/tools/validation_store/validation_store.py
answers.how: Both seal writers (cairn test --seal in cli.py main, cairn test --reseal via reseal.reseal_all) read the standing record's evidence.hollow keys before the run and again after the persist; the difference is printed as a HOLLOW VOIDED block naming each ticket and `cairn test --hollow <t> --seal`. Printed, never refused: a reseal over moved code is legitimate and the reading expiring is right (Law 3).
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces: a reading silently dropped is a quiet error); Law 1 (five tickets re-derived the same diagnosis at FIXME).
answers.what: A seal that replaces a validation a hollow reading was taken over names each ticket whose reading it voided and says to retake it after PROVEME, so the next PROVED crossing is not the first place the loss is seen.

bullets.text: A reseal over moved code drops every hollow reading on that proof, correctly, and said nothing. n=5 tickets bounced to FIXME on hollow_evidence_absent tonight. The seal writers now print which tickets lost their reading and the command to retake it.
